Repo: /opt/nxeon-staging-hostnamefix (a git worktree of the Nxeon Next.js/Prisma VPS hosting platform — read-only exploration, do not edit anything).

Context: The Prisma model `Server.hostname` is a plain `hostname String` with NO uniqueness constraint. VPS checkout hardcodes "web-01" as the default hostname (components/nx/order.tsx lines ~185 and ~511), and DeployView.tsx shows it as a placeholder too. A production incident happened when a hostname-based lookup `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: 'web-01' } })` grabbed the WRONG customer's server (cross-customer data leak of SSH port/status).

I need two exhaustive lists, each with exact file path + line number + a short code snippet for every hit:

LIST A — every place in the codebase (app/, components/, lib/, server actions, API routes, scripts/) that ASSIGNS a default or placeholder hostname value during server/VPS/game-server creation or checkout. Include both the VPS path (components/nx/order.tsx, components/nx/DeployView.tsx) and search for the SAME pattern in game-server checkout/provisioning code — search for things like default hostname strings (e.g. "web-01", "mc-01", "game-01", or similar), `hostname:` assignments, `.trim() || ` fallback patterns, hostname generation helper functions, provisioning/deploy server actions under app/api or app/actions or lib/ related to VPS or game server creation.

LIST B — every place in the codebase that does a database lookup KEYED ON hostname — i.e. any `findFirst`, `findUnique`, `findMany`, raw SQL, or Prisma query with a `where` clause containing `hostname` on the Server model (or any related model). For each hit, note: (1) the exact query, (2) whether it is already scoped/filtered by userId/accountId/session or by server id in the same where clause or an outer check, (3) the calling context (e.g. support/admin tool, customer-facing API route, cron/automation, internal script) so I can judge whether cross-customer data exposure is possible.

Also check: is `hostname` used anywhere for actual DNS records, nginx/vhost config, reverse-proxy routing, or Traefik/Caddy labels — i.e. does anything outside the Server model's own row treat hostname as a globally-namespaced identifier (which would argue for GLOBAL uniqueness), or is it purely a cosmetic customer-facing label scoped to their own account (which would argue for PER-ACCOUNT uniqueness)? Search for "hostname" usage in any DNS provisioning code, nginx config generation, docker/container naming, or subdomain generation.

Also note the exact Prisma model definition for Server (full field list, especially id, userId/accountId equivalent field name, hostname, and any existing @@unique or @unique attributes on the model) from prisma/schema.prisma.

Report back as plain text with the two lists (file:line + snippet each) and the DNS/vhost findings and the Server model definition. Do not truncate — I need every hit, not just examples. This is for a real production security fix so completeness matters more than brevity.

744:   //     been given a chance to act on.
745:   // (2) `renewNow` auto-unsuspended ANY suspended server on payment, so a spammer
746:   //     suspended for outbound abuse could pay and put themselves straight back
747:   //     on the network.
748:   // Both now scope strictly to UNPAID.

750:   // Human-readable reason a PROVISION failed terminally, set by the worker on the

780:   // renews (commitRenewal), so each cycle can remind at most once. Null = not yet
781:   // reminded this cycle.
782:   renewalReminderSentAt DateTime?

784:   updatedAt             DateTime            @updatedAt

786:   user                  User                @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
787:   nodeId                String?
788:   node                  Node?               @relation(fields: [nodeId], references: [id])

790:   bwOutBytes            BigInt              @default(0)
791:   abuseBwMark           BigInt? // last bwOutBytes sample, for outbound-rate abuse detection
792:   abuseBwMarkAt         DateTime? // when abuseBwMark was taken
793:   bwWindowStart         DateTime            @default(now())
794:   termMonths            Int                 @default(1) // 1=monthly, 12=annual, 24=biennial, 36=triennial
795:   /// PERCENT OFF the term-discounted monthly rate that the months currently sitting
796:   /// between `now` and `expiresAt` were ACTUALLY sold at. This is the rate basis
797:   /// every proration must price against (lib/proration.ts).
798:   ///
799:   /// WHY IT EXISTS (2026-07-26). `prorateDeltaCents` defaulted its rate basis to
800:   /// `currentPromo(now)` — whatever seasonal promo happened to be running at the
801:   /// instant a resize was priced. Promos rotate by calendar date from a 15% Launch
802:   /// Sale to 45% for Cyber Monday, so a customer could upgrade during Cyber Monday
803:   /// (delta priced at 55% of the honest rate, small charge) and downgrade during
804:   /// the Launch Sale (delta priced at 85%, large credit) and pocket the 30-point
805:   /// spread x plan delta x every remaining month — repeatable every promo cycle,
806:   /// self-service, with the platform's own marketing calendar as the schedule.
807:   /// lib/promotions.ts is explicit that a promo is a FIRST-TERM intro discount that
808:   /// renewals never receive, so pricing a mid-term change off today's promo was
809:   /// wrong even before it was exploitable.
810:   ///
811:   /// WHY A PERCENT AND NOT A CENTS RATE. Proration is a DIFFERENCE between two
812:   /// plans' rates. A stored $/mo figure prices only the plan the server is on and
813:   /// says nothing about the plan it is moving to, so the other half of the
814:   /// subtraction would still need a basis invented for it — which is the bug. A
815:   /// percent is a rate BASIS that applies to any plan price, so both halves of the
816:   /// delta come from this one persisted number and the round trip is symmetric by
817:   /// construction rather than by convention. It also survives a plan change with no
818:   /// write at all: the customer keeps the rate they bought at, so up-then-down is
819:   /// exactly zero.
820:   ///
821:   ///   0   = full price. What BOTH renewal paths bill (worker/billing.ts sweep and
822:   ///         lib/actions.ts renewNow charge `vpsTermPriceCents` with no promo), and
823:   ///         what a flat-priced game plan is sold at.
824:   ///   1-99= a genuine intro/seasonal discount, or a blend of paid and gifted
825:   ///         months (see prorateBlendPercent in lib/proration.ts).
826:   ///   100 = gifted. Nothing was paid for these months, so nothing may prorate out
827:   ///         of them — an admin extension/free grant records this.
828:   ///   NULL= unknown. Only on rows that predate this column; resolved by an
829:   ///         EXPLICIT conservative fallback (`resolveTermPromoPercent`), never by
830:   ///         falling through to today's promo, because that IS the bug above.
831:   ///
832:   /// FLOAT, not Int, even though every promo in the catalogue is a whole number.
833:   /// Blending a renewal into a part-used term lands on halves: 36 months at 45% off
834:   /// plus 36 renewed at full price is exactly 22.5% off, and rounding that to 23
835:   /// quietly shaves $7.20 off a $1,071.36 credit. A first term still stores the

# Hostname Uniqueness Security Review — Findings

## Server model definition (prisma/schema.prisma, lines 707–984)

```prisma
model Server {
  id                    String              @id @default(cuid())
  uptimeDays            ServerUptimeDaily[]
  name                  String
  label                 String?             // customer-facing nickname (rename)
  partnerSource         String?
  hostname              String              // <-- NO @unique, NO @@unique, plain String
  vmid                  Int?                @unique
  status                ServerStatus        @default(PENDING)
  ipAddress             String?             @unique
  sshPort               Int?                @unique
  rootPassword          String?
  rootPasswordEnc       String?
  ...
  subdomain             String?             @unique   // Minecraft <sub>.play.nxeon.cloud
  ...
  userId                String
  user                  User                @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  nodeId                String?
  node                  Node?               @relation(fields: [nodeId], references: [id])
  ...
  customDomain          String?
  customDomainVerified  Boolean             @default(false)
  ...
  telemetryTokenHash    String?             @unique
  telemetryEvents       TelemetryEvent[]
}
```

Key facts:
- `hostname String` — **no `@unique`, no `@@unique` compound involving it anywhere in the model.**
- The account-scoping field is **`userId`** (`String`, FK to `User`). Every legitimate lookup must filter on this (or on `id`, which is globally unique) to be safely scoped.
- By contrast, `vmid`, `ipAddress`, `sshPort`, `subdomain`, and `telemetryTokenHash` **do** carry `@unique` — `hostname` is conspicuously the odd one out among identifier-shaped fields.
- `customDomain` also has no DB-level `@unique`, but (see below) has an application-level uniqueness *check* before write, because it's DNS-relevant. `hostname` has neither a DB constraint nor an app-level check.

Related model confirming the platform *does* know how to do this correctly when something is genuinely DNS-namespaced:
```prisma
model HostingHostnameClaim {          // prisma/schema.prisma:1983
  id        String           @id @default(cuid())
  hostname  String           @unique  // <-- real global uniqueness, for the shared-hosting product
  accountId String
  account   HostingAccount   @relation(fields: [accountId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  kind      HostingClaimKind
}
```
```prisma
model NxCloudInstance {               // prisma/schema.prisma:5784
  subdomain    String  @unique
  customDomain String? @unique
}
```

---

## LIST A — every place a default/placeholder hostname is ASSIGNED during server/VPS/game-server creation

### Live VPS checkout (currently-wired route: `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` → `DeployView`)
1. **components/nx/order.tsx:185**
   ```ts
   hostname: k === "vps" ? "web-01" : "",
   ```
   `seedOrder()` — every fresh VPS order in wizard state starts with the literal string `"web-01"`.

2. **components/nx/order.tsx:511**
   ```ts
   hostname: o.hostname.trim() || "web-01",
   ```
   Live-quote call (`quoteOrder`) — if the customer clears the field, `"web-01"` is silently substituted before pricing.

3. **components/nx/DeployView.tsx:909**
   ```ts
   : o.hostname.trim() || "web-01"}
   ```
   Cart/review-step summary label — same fallback shown to the customer as their server's name.

4. **components/nx/DeployView.tsx:1649**
   ```ts
   sub={[o.hostname.trim() || "web-01", cat.oses.find((x) => x.id === o.osId)?.name].filter(Boolean).join(" · ")}>
   ```
   Collapsed "Server settings" fold subtitle — same fallback.

5. **components/nx/DeployView.tsx:1656**
   ```ts
   spellCheck={false} autoComplete="off" placeholder="web-01"
   ```
   The actual `<input>` placeholder text for the hostname field.

6. **lib/order.ts:86–89 / :259 / :981** — the field that actually reaches the DB:
   ```ts
   // lib/order.ts:86 (orderSchema, Zod)
   hostname: z.string().min(3).max(40).regex(/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/i, "Hostname: letters, digits, hyphens"),
   // lib/order.ts:259 (intentFromFormData)

   // lib/order.ts:981 (placeOrder, tx.server.create data)
   name: intent.hostname,
   hostname: intent.hostname,
   ```
   No collision/uniqueness check is performed on `intent.hostname` anywhere in this function before `tx.server.create`. Since the wizard defaults/falls back to `"web-01"` and a large fraction of customers never touch the field, many rows are expected to literally collide on `hostname = "web-01"`.

### Game-server checkout (same live `DeployView.tsx`, game branch → `lib/actions-gameplans.ts` → `lib/game-order.ts`)
7. **lib/game-order.ts:103** (`gameIntentFromFormData`)
   ```ts
   hostname: String(formData.get("hostname") ?? "").trim() || undefined,
   ```
8. **lib/game-order.ts:117–120** — hostname-generation helper:

   /** Short random suffix so auto-generated hostnames don't collide. */
   export function randSuffix(n = 6): string {
     return Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 2 + n);

9. **lib/game-order.ts:277–286** (`gameOrderQuote`) — the actual default-assignment logic:
   ```ts
   const rawHost = (intent.hostname ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
   let hostname = rawHost;
   if (hostname === "") {
     hostname = `${gp.gameFamily}-${randSuffix()}`;      // e.g. "minecraft-x7f3k2"
   } else if (!(hostname.length >= 3 && hostname.length <= 40 && HOSTNAME_RE.test(hostname))) {
     throw new GameOrderError(...);
   }
   ```
   Uses `Math.random()` (not crypto-random) and **is never checked against the DB for collision** before insert — lower collision probability than `"web-01"` (36^6 ≈ 2.2B combinations) but still theoretically possible, and by design (not accidental like "web-01").
10. **lib/game-order.ts:649–650** (`placeGameOrder`, `tx.server.create` data):

12. **lib/actions.ts:1243–1266** (`adminGrantFreeVps`, admin-only action):
    ```ts
    hostname: z.string().min(3).max(40).regex(/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/i),
    ...
    const server = await db.server.create({
      data: {
        name: parsed.data.hostname,
        hostname: parsed.data.hostname,
        ...
    ```
    Admin types an arbitrary hostname for a gifted VPS; no uniqueness check against existing `Server.hostname` rows.

13. **lib/actions.ts:490** (`previewOrderCoupon`):
    ```ts
    hostname: "preview-host",
    ```
    Placeholder used only to satisfy `orderQuote`'s required param for a dry-run price preview — never written to the DB, so low risk, but literally another shared/reusable magic-string default, and demonstrates the pattern is copy-pasted throughout the codebase.

14. **scripts/e2e-test.ts:34–41** (`tx.server.create`):
    ```ts
    const s = await tx.server.create({
      data: {
        name: "e2e-test",
        hostname: "e2e-test",
        ...
    ```
    Hardcoded literal in an E2E test/seed script; re-running the script (or running it against a non-empty DB) will create additional rows with the exact same `hostname`.

### Newer/dead-code checkout path (NOT currently wired to any route — see note below)
15. **components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:126–145** — this path uses a materially *better* pattern than the live one:
    ```ts
    function randHostSuffix() {
      return Math.random().toString(36).replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, "").slice(0, 4).padEnd(3, "0");
    }
    function defaultHostnameFor(image: Image | undefined, suffix: string) {
      const base = (image?.family ?? "").toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, "").slice(0, 24);
      const stem = base.length >= 2 ? base : "nxeon";
      return `${stem}-${suffix}`;   // e.g. "ubuntu-0k4f", "debian-9c1"
    }
    ```
    and `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:580–586` applies it via `useEffect`. **However**, `DeployWizard.tsx` / `DeployHub.tsx` / `GameDeployWizard.tsx` are **not imported by any file under `app/`** — a comment in the live file confirms this explicitly: `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:327` — *"...calls it, same as the old wizard's DeployHub did..."*. This is dead code from a previous wizard iteration, not reachable from any route today. Flagging for completeness since it still matches the "default hostname" search, but it is not part of the live attack surface.

---

## LIST B — every DB lookup KEYED ON `hostname`

### 1. **The exact incident-class pattern: singleton infrastructure lookups on `hostname: "freemc-host"`**
This exact anti-pattern (`findFirst({ where: { hostname: <literal> } })`, unscoped by any other field) appears **7 times**, all resolving the one dedicated free-Minecraft Docker host row, and all returning **SSH credentials** (`rootPassword`, `rootPasswordEnc`, `sshPort`) for whatever row hostname matching happens to return:

| File:Line | Query | Scoped by userId/id? | Calling context |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts:65-68` | `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: {..., rootPassword, rootPasswordEnc, sshPort, dedicatedIp, node...} })` | No | Customer-facing server actions (`"use server"` file) — every export is a public authenticated endpoint |
| `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts:25-28` | same shape | No | Admin-only tool (`requireArea("fleet")` gated at call sites) |
| `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts:128-131` | same shape | No | Customer-facing (LuckPerms role management) |
| `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts:44-47` | same shape | No | Customer-facing (inventory/item commands) |
| `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts:47-50` | same shape | No | Customer-facing (world-switch actions) |
| `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts:41-44` | same shape | No | Customer-facing (mod install) |
| `app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]/page.tsx:91-94` | `db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: {..., rootPassword, rootPasswordEnc, sshPort, dedicatedIp} })` | No | **Public, unauthenticated marketing page** (best-effort live status widget) |

**Exposure analysis**: this is not scoped by `userId` because it's intentionally looking up shared infrastructure, not a customer's own row — but it is looking up that infrastructure **by `hostname` alone, on a field with no DB uniqueness constraint**, exactly the pattern that caused the incident. `hostname` is customer-editable free text at VPS/game order time (`lib/order.ts:86-89`, `lib/game-order.ts:278-286`) with no reserved-word blocklist found anywhere in the validation (`HOSTNAME_RE`/`orderSchema` only check character shape, 3–40 chars). **If any customer's own VPS or game order happens to end up with `hostname = "freemc-host"`** (typed deliberately, or coincidentally, since nothing reserves it), `findFirst` has no defined ordering guarantee and could return that customer's `Server` row instead of the real internal host. Consequences: (a) if the customer's row sorts first, every one of the 7 call sites above starts SSH-ing into a **customer's VPS with commands meant for the internal Docker fleet** (`docker exec`, `docker restart`, `docker rm -f`, RCON), and (b) the real internal host's `rootPassword`/`rootPasswordEnc`/`sshPort` become unreachable (denial of service to the whole free-Minecraft fleet) or, worse, **the marketing page or another customer inadvertently gets shown/uses the SSH credentials of whichever row won the race**.

### 2. **Operator/CLI script — unscoped, non-deterministic**
**scripts/backfill-claude.ts:88-91**
```ts
const asVmid = Number(arg);
servers = await db.server.findMany({
  where: Number.isInteger(asVmid) ? { vmid: asVmid } : { hostname: arg },
  select: SELECT,
});
```
- Query: `findMany` (not even `findFirst`) on `{ hostname: arg }` where `arg` is an operator-typed CLI argument (`npx tsx scripts/backfill-claude.ts <hostname|vmid>`).
- Scoping: **none** — no `userId`, no `id`.
- Context: internal ops/automation script (`Claude Code backfill onto existing servers via SSH`). If an operator runs it with `web-01` (a highly likely value given the checkout default in List A #1–6), it will match **every customer server still named "web-01"** and run the backfill's SSH/cloud-init installation flow against **all of them in one invocation** — a script intended for one target server silently fans out across customers.

### 3. **Portal-wide search — partially scoped**
**app/api/search/route.ts:48-49**
```ts
const own = isAdmin ? {} : { userId: user.id };
...
db.server.findMany({
  where: { OR: [{ hostname: like }, { label: like }, { name: like }], ...own },
  include: { user: true },
  take: 6,
}),
```
- Scoped by `userId` for ordinary customers (`own = { userId: user.id }` when not admin) — safe for that role.
- **Unscoped for admins** (`own = {}`) — by design, this is the global admin search (`⌘K` "Search anything"), intentionally cross-account; not a bug per se, but confirms `hostname` is treated as a searchable-but-not-unique field, and an admin typing a common default like `web-01` gets a a mixed bag of unrelated customers' servers with no indication in the UI that the match isn't unique.

### 4. **NAT/rehearsal/admin tooling — id-scoped, hostname only used for display/logging (safe, listed for completeness)**
These `findUnique`/`findMany` calls select `hostname` alongside `id`, but the `where` clause itself keys on `id`, `vmid`, or another indexed unique field — **not** on `hostname` — so they are not the vulnerable pattern, just consumers of the field for logs/labels:
- `worker/index.ts:2428`, `:2285-2287`, `:2357-2359` — `where: { id: job.serverId }`, hostname only in `select`.
- `worker/services.ts:151` — same shape.
- `worker/game-update.ts:167` — `where` not shown keyed on hostname (id/status-based).
- `scripts/migration-rehearsal.ts:164` — `where: { id: targetId }`.
- `app/admin/*/page.tsx` (servers, migrations, abuse, monitoring, provisioning, jobs, ips, products, games, email-templates) — all read paths, `where` keyed on `id: { in: ... }` or no filter (admin fleet-wide listing pages, which are supposed to be cross-account for staff), `hostname` only ever in `select`/display. Confirmed safe as **read/display**, not identity-resolution.
- `app/dashboard/*/page.tsx` (billing, ssl, servers, volumes, nxlabs, claude-code, migrate/consolidate) — all scoped by `userId` in `where`, `hostname` only in `select`/display.

### 5. Raw SQL
No `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` calls reference `hostname` anywhere in the codebase (`grep` of every `$queryRaw`/`$executeRaw` call site returned none touching `hostname`).

### 6. `findUnique` on hostname
None exist and none *can* exist without a Prisma error — `findUnique` requires a `@unique`/`@id` field, and `hostname` has neither, so every hostname-keyed lookup in the codebase is necessarily `findFirst` or `findMany`, both of which return **whichever matching row Postgres/Prisma happens to return first** when duplicates exist (no defined tie-break) — this is mechanically identical to the incident's `findFirst({ where: { hostname: 'web-01' } })`.

---

## DNS / vhost / nginx / Traefik / Docker — is `Server.hostname` globally namespaced anywhere?

**No.** `Server.hostname` (the VPS/game-server product) is **not** consumed by any DNS, reverse-proxy, or vhost-generation code path. Specifically:

- **Proxmox VM clone**: `worker/index.ts:848-850` sets `name: server.hostname` on the Proxmox clone API call — this becomes the **hypervisor's own VM display name**, keyed internally by `vmid` (which *is* `@unique`), not by name. Two VMs can have identical Proxmox `name` values with zero functional conflict.
- **Cloud-init config** (`worker/index.ts:989-1010`, the `cfg` object passed to Proxmox's cloud-init API): sets `ciuser`, `cipassword`, `sshkeys`, `nameserver: "1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8"` (public DNS *resolvers* the guest uses, unrelated to the guest's own name), `onboot`, `cicustom` — **no explicit `hostname:`/cloud-init key is set from `server.hostname`.** Whatever OS-level hostname ends up inside the guest is Proxmox's own default derivation from the VM `name` field — it is local to that one guest's `/etc/hostname`, never published anywhere, and two guests sharing it has no observable effect on each other.
- **`lib/sftp.ts:232`** (`"hostname": file("nxeon-vps\n")`) is part of the **SANDBOX-mode simulated filesystem** (`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, staging-only fake SFTP tree) — not real guest state, not derived from `Server.hostname` at all, irrelevant to production DNS/vhost behavior.
- **Docker `--hostname` flags** (`prisma/seed-wave8-games.ts:86`, `prisma/seed-blog-wave3-wave4-games.ts:419`, `prisma/seed-wave3-games.ts:59`) set the *container's* internal hostname to a **static literal per game** (e.g. `--hostname nightingale`, `--hostname icarus`) baked into the game's catalog `setupScript` — unrelated to `Server.hostname`, and scoped to one container's own network namespace.

**What *is* actually treated as globally/DNS-namespaced, and correctly guarded, are two entirely different fields:**

1. **`Server.customDomain`** (`String?`, no `@unique` in schema, but enforced at the application layer):
   `lib/actions-game-control.ts:1224-1227` (`setCustomDomain`):
   ```ts
   const existing = await db.server.findFirst({
     where: { customDomain: v.domain, id: { not: serverId } },
     select: { id: true },
   });
   if (existing) return { ok: false, error: "This domain is already in use on another server." };
   ```
   This *is* fed into real DNS/reachability verification (`verifyCustomDomainDns`, `lib/actions-game-control.ts:1270`) and is deliberately checked for cross-account collision before being written — the correct pattern the codebase already knows how to apply, just never applied to `hostname`.

2. **`Server.subdomain`** (`String? @unique` in schema, for Minecraft `<sub>.play.nxeon.cloud` SRV records) — additionally cross-checked at the application layer against the separate `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` table in `lib/game-subdomain.ts:14-28` (`isSubdomainAvailable`), since Postgres can't enforce a unique constraint across two tables.

3. **`HostingHostnameClaim.hostname`** (`String @unique`, `prisma/schema.prisma:1985`) — the real hosting/cPanel-style product's vhost hostnames (primary domain / subdomains / addon domains), consumed throughout `worker/hosting.ts` (vhost creation, `resolveInstallTarget`, wildcard cert coverage, thumbnail capture) — globally unique by DB constraint, exactly the pattern `Server.hostname` lacks.

4. **`NxCloudInstance.subdomain` / `.customDomain`** (`prisma/schema.prisma:5797-5798`) — both `@unique` at the DB level.

**Conclusion for the uniqueness-scope question**: `Server.hostname` is purely a cosmetic, customer-facing label (dashboard display, email templates, terminal-session labels, backup/log messages) with no DNS, nginx, Traefik/Caddy, or Docker-networking role of its own — it is never resolved, never routed to, never certificate-checked. This argues for **per-account uniqueness at most** (or simply no uniqueness requirement at all, purely presentational) as the correct long-term product semantics — **but every lookup that currently treats it as if it *were* globally unique (List B, especially the 7 `"freemc-host"` sites and the `scripts/backfill-claude.ts` CLI tool) is the actual bug surface**, since those call sites assume single-row resolution that the schema never guaranteed and that customer-controlled input (List A) can collide with, either accidentally (`"web-01"` being the literal default nearly every VPS customer leaves untouched) or adversarially (a customer deliberately naming their server `freemc-host`).
